title: Ep 822: How To Win Investment For Employer Branding
guest: Stephen Quinn, CEO of Atomic (an insight-led agency working with employer brand leaders)
vendor_flag: Guest is the CEO of the agency (Atomic) whose own diagnostic tool and client roster are discussed at length in the interview; treat metrics framework as vendor-sourced, not independently verified.
angle: Gives TA leaders sitting in employer brand a concrete stakeholder-metrics list (cost per qualified lead, decline reduction, referral rate, ROI) to take into a budget conversation.

points.claim: Stop reporting vanity content metrics to the CFO; they land badly and don't justify budget.
points.evidence: example figures: 'X thousand likes and 4,000 views'
points.quote: my LinkedIn campaign or my YouTube campaign delivered X thousand likes and 4,000 views

points.claim: Track five specific employer-brand metrics that actually resonate with finance: cost per qualified lead, time to hire, decline reduction, referral rates, and ROI of program investments.
points.evidence: Atomic Diagnostic framework; named metrics: cost per qualified lead, time to hire, reduction in declines, referral rates, ROI of program investments
points.quote: cost per qualified lead will be a classic one... Time to hire is fairly standard... reduction in declines

points.claim: Benchmark employer brand health against a structured scorecard before building a roadmap, not just launching campaigns.
points.evidence: 32 measures used in Atomic's client diagnostic, self-scored plus external analysis
points.quote: we have 32 measures that we can score against

points.claim: Match the format of your business case to the audience: spreadsheets for finance, not slide decks.
points.evidence: named functions: HR vs finance reporting preference
points.quote: HR thinks in PowerPoints and finance think in spreadsheets

points.claim: Reduced employer-brand headcount is a widespread pattern worth naming to stakeholders when arguing for resource.
points.evidence: described drop from five-to-seven person teams down to two
points.quote: maybe there was five, six, seven people in a team, maybe they're down to two

title: Episoe 046: The AI Reckoning in HR Tech w/ George LaRocque & Brandon Jeffs
guest: George LaRocque, founder and principal analyst of WorkTech (an HR tech advisory and market intelligence firm)
vendor_flag: Guest is an independent analyst, not a vendor for a product being demoed; no product pitch present, but he does reference his own firm's research/pitchfest involvement, worth noting as a light bias.
angle: Warns TA leaders buying or piloting AI tools that pilot pricing is often subsidized and real costs could rise sharply, and flags the compliance risk of DIY vibe-coded HR tools at scale.

points.claim: Treat cheap AI tool pilots with caution: token costs for HR tech are currently subsidized by AI labs and may rise sharply once vendors need to recoup real costs.
points.evidence: comparison: sales/go-to-market AI infrastructure can cost up to 10 times more than recruiting tech's historic cost base
points.quote: built on the same infrastructure as say sales and go to market tech, which can be up to 10 times more expensive

points.claim: Building your own recruiting tools in Claude or similar can work for a solo recruiter or small team, but becomes risky once you operate across multiple locations or as a government contractor.
points.quote: you can build something really cool in Claude or Lovable or what have you and get 80%

points.claim: Before buying a new point-solution AI tool, check your existing ATS or CRM roadmap first, since many gaps will be filled natively within a quarter or two.
points.evidence: recommendation to check vendor roadmap timing: 'next quarter or two'
points.quote: I would really listen to them about where they're headed in the next quarter or two

points.claim: The ATS market is expected to roughly double to two-and-a-half times in market cap within the next several years, meaning more vendor investment and choice is coming.
points.evidence: figure: ATS market poised to grow about 2 to 2.5x in market cap in next 4 to 6 years
points.quote: The ATS market is poised to grow about 2 to 2.5x in market cap in the next 4 to 6 years

points.claim: When picking new recruiting tech, talk to your peer network before buying, since referrals carry more real signal than vendor hype on LinkedIn.
points.evidence: named channel: LinkedIn vendor commentary contrasted with peer referrals
points.quote: talking to their network, talking who's doing what, what's working, what isn't

title: Brainfood Live On Air - Ep404 - In Conversation with John Vlastelica
guest: John Vlastelica, founder of Recruiting Toolbox (recruiting consulting and training firm); former head of tech recruiting at Amazon and head of recruiting at Expedia
vendor_flag: Not a product demo. Guest runs a consulting/training firm (Recruiting Toolbox) but is not selling a specific tool here; his frameworks (e.g. the five-level talent advisor model) are his own IP, promoted partly to drive attendance at a paid conference (Recfest Nashville) where he says the full framework will be shared.
angle: Gives TA leaders a concrete self-assessment ladder (level 1 to 5 talent advisor) and a language for defending headcount and inefficiency to finance during budget season, both usable this week.

points.claim: Use the five-level talent-advisor framework to place yourself and your recruiters and plan what to level up next, from basic intake-taking to shaping org strategy.
points.evidence: named levels 1 through 5, with level 5 estimated at fewer than 1 in 50 recruiters
points.quote: I would bet less than one in 50 recruiters will ever get to this point

points.claim: Roughly a quarter of corporate recruiters currently operate as true talent advisors, so most TA teams have real room to grow into the role.
points.quote: maybe 25% of corporate recruiters are operating as talent advisors
points.note: guest caveats this as a rough, possibly generous estimate, not a survey figure

points.claim: Going into budget season, be ready to argue that AI doubling recruiter productivity does not simply mean halving the team, because high-touch inefficient work for hard-to-fill roles is a feature, not a bug.
points.evidence: direct guidance for budget season conversations with finance
points.quote: we have to be able to explain inefficiency as a feature not a bug

points.claim: One client's in-house TA function has been cut through 14 waves of layoffs, from 700 people down to a skeleton team, illustrating how far TA headcount has fallen at some large companies.
points.evidence: figures: 700 people down to roughly two, across 14 waves of layoffs
points.quote: one client who had 700 people in their corporate TA function that is down to two something right now

points.claim: Interviewing 10 candidates to fill a $60,000-a-year role is a concrete, quotable example of funnel waste to bring to hiring managers as a business case for change.
points.quote: someone had to interview 10 candidates to fill a $60,000 a year job
